From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Gamba, gambá, gambă, and gâmba

English

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From viola da gamba, ultimately from Italian gamba (“leg”). Doublet of gam, gamb, jamb, and jambe.

Noun

[edit]

gamba (plural gambas) (music)

  1. Abbreviation of viola da gamba.
  2. A rank of organ pipes, so called for a supposed resemblance of the sound to that of a viola da gamba.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin gamba (“leg”); compare gambol. Doublet of gam, gamb, jamb, and jambe.

Noun

[edit]

gamba

  1. (anatomy) The metacarpus or metatarsus of ruminants, etc.
Related terms
[edit]
Etymologically related terms
  • gamb
  • gambade, gambado
  • gambit
  • gambol
  • gambrel
  • viola da gamba, gambist

Etymology 3

[edit]

Alteration of gamble.

Noun

[edit]

gamba (countable and uncountable, plural gambas)

  1. (Twitch-speak) Gambling.
    Start a prediction on it. We want gamba!

Noun

[edit]

  1. water

    Latin

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    Etymology

    [edit]

      Borrowed from Ancient Greek καμπή (kampḗ, “fixture, bend, winding”).

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈɡam.ba]
      • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈɡam.ba]

      Noun

      [edit]

      gamba f (genitive gambae); first declension

      1. (Late Latin) (of animals) hock, shank
      2. (Medieval Latin) (upper part of) leg, thigh

      Declension

      [edit]

      nominative gamba gambae

      vocative gamba gambae

      Spanish

      [edit]

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /ˈɡamba/ [ˈɡãm.ba]
      • Audio (Venezuela):(file)
      • Rhymes: -amba
      • Syllabification: gam‧ba

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

      Borrowed from Catalan gamba, from Late Latin *gambarus, from Latin gammarus / cammarus (“lobster”), from Ancient Greek κάμμαρος (kámmaros). Sense 3 comes from the old 100 Chilean pesos banknote having the color of a shrimp.

      Noun

      [edit]

      gamba f (plural gambas)

      1. (Spain) shrimp
        Synonym: camarón (Latin America)
      2. (Spain, derogatory slang) butterface, prawn
      3. (Chile, colloquial) 100 pesos
      Derived terms
      [edit]
      • hombre gamba
      • mujer gamba

      Etymology 2

      [edit]

        Borrowed from Italian gamba, from Late Latin[1] or Vulgar Latin[2] gamba, camba (“leg”), from Ancient Greek καμπή (kampḗ, “bending”).

        Noun

        [edit]

        gamba f (plural gambas)

        1. (Argentina, colloquial) leg
          Synonym: pierna
        2. (Chile, colloquial) human foot
          Synonym: pie
        Related terms
        [edit]
        • hacer la gamba
        • meter la gamba
        • viola de gamba

        References

        2. ^ “gamba”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

        Tooro

        [edit]

        Etymology

        [edit]

        Inherited from Proto-Bantu *-gàmba (“to speak; to answer”).

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
        • IPA(key): /ɡáːmba/

        Verb

        [edit]

        -gamba (infinitive okugamba)

        1. (ambitransitive) to say, to speak
        2. (intransitive) to make a noise:
          1. (of a bird) to cry
          2. (of furniture) to creak
          3. (of a drum) to sound
          4. (of a bell) to ring
          5. (of a gun) to go off

        Derived terms

        [edit]
        • Verbal derivations:
          • Applicative: -gambira
          • Long causative: -gambisa
          • Passive: -gambwa
        • Nominal derivations:
          • ekigambo (“word”)
          • engamba (“way of speaking”)
          • omugambi (“speaker”)
          • orugambo (“rumor”)
